museo-archeologico-nazionale-dell-antica.description: State archaeology museum in Alife, Campania, devoted to Allifae, the Roman-era walled town on whose remains the modern settlement stands. It displays archaeological finds recovered from excavations in the surrounding territory.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-della-basil.name: "Dinu Adamesteanu" National Archaeological Museum of Basilicata
museo-archeologico-nazionale-della-basil.description: National archaeological museum of the Basilicata region, inaugurated in 2005 and named after Dinu Adamesteanu, the Romanian archaeologist who served as the region's first superintendent from 1964 to 1977. It occupies Palazzo Loffredo, built by the Guevara family in the late 15th century, and displays finds from the Enotri, Greek, Apulian, Peuketiantes, Lucanian and Roman periods.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-della-lomel.name: National Archaeological Museum of the Lomellina
museo-archeologico-nazionale-della-lomel.description: National archaeological museum of the Lomellina area, inaugurated in 1998 inside the Sforza Castle of Vigevano, in a stable block commissioned by Gian Galeazzo Visconti and designed by Maffeo da Como in the 1470s. The collection covers roughly 2000 BC to 800 AD and includes the Strada Collection of glassware, notably a signed 1st-century cup by the glassmaker Aristeas.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-della-sirit.name: National Archaeological Museum of the Siritide - Policoro
museo-archeologico-nazionale-della-sirit.description: National archaeological museum inaugurated in 1969 within the Heraclea archaeological site near Policoro. It presents material from the Neolithic to the Roman period, including pottery, bronzes and votive figures from the Greek colonies of Siris and Heraclea alongside finds from the indigenous Oenotrian and Lucanian populations.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-della-valle.name: National Archaeological Museum of the Valle Camonica
museo-archeologico-nazionale-della-valle.description: National archaeological museum of the Valle Camonica, opened in 1981 and relocated in 2021 to a former convent in Cividate Camuno beside the Roman amphitheatre. Its four sections trace Roman settlement of the valley through inscriptions, sculpture and everyday objects, including material from the Sanctuary of Minerva.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-della-valle.name: National Archaeological Museum of the Sarno Valley
museo-archeologico-nazionale-della-valle.description: National archaeological museum inaugurated in 2011 to house finds from excavations conducted across the Sarno Valley since 1970, spanning prehistory to the Middle Ages. Housed in Palazzo Capua, the collection includes Samnite funerary assemblages, painted stone coffin burials of the 4th century BC, and bronze and silver jewellery from the 8th-7th centuries BC.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-delle-march.name: National Archaeological Museum of the Marche
museo-archeologico-nazionale-delle-march.description: National archaeological museum of the Marche region, founded in 1863 and installed since 1958 in the 16th-century Palazzo Ferretti, whose monumental staircase was designed by Luigi Vanvitelli. Its holdings centre on the Picene civilisation of the 9th-4th centuries BC, alongside Greek, Gallic and Roman material and a numismatic collection of some 90,000 coins.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-dell-antica.name: National Archaeological Museum of Ancient Capua
museo-archeologico-nazionale-dell-antica.description: National archaeological museum inaugurated in 1995 to display finds from ancient Capua, spanning the Iron Age through the Etruscan, Samnite and Roman periods. It occupies a 19th-century former cavalry barracks built over the remains of the ancient Capitolium and incorporating the medieval Torre di Sant'Erasmo, with ceramics, bronzes, mosaics and funerary goods from the Capua excavations.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-adria.name: National Archaeological Museum of Adria
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-adria.description: National archaeological museum established in 1903 by the municipality of Adria around the Bocchi family collection, and housed since 1961 in a purpose-built structure designed by architect Giambattista Scarpari, expanded with a curved new wing between 2002 and 2009. It preserves pre-Roman and Roman finds from the area, notably the Tomb of the Biga, a 3rd-century BC chariot burial with three horses.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-altino.name: National Archaeological Museum of Altino
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-altino.description: National archaeological museum dedicated to the Veneto-Roman settlement of Altino, first opened in 1960 and rehoused in 2015 in a converted 19th-century rice mill designed by architect Stefano Filippi, with an observation tower over the Venetian lagoon. Its more than 40,000 objects span the 8th century BC to the 5th century AD and include prehistoric wooden artefacts, Roman glass and horse burial equipment.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-amendola.name: National Archaeological Museum of Amendolara
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-amendola.description: National archaeological museum of Amendolara, also known as the Vincenzo Laviola museum, established in 1996 around Laviola's private collection together with material excavated at Colle San Nicola. Its four sections cover protohistory, the archaic and classical Magna Graecia periods and the Byzantine era, with pottery, metal tools and jewellery from the 12th century BC alongside Greek ceramics of the 8th-6th centuries BC.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-aquileia.name: National Archaeological Museum of Aquileia
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-aquileia.description: National archaeological museum established in 1882 by the Austrian authorities, building on an 18th-century collection formed by Canon Gian Domenico Bertoli. Housed in Villa Cassis Faraone, with porticoed lapidary galleries added in 1898, it preserves statues, household and decorative objects, gems, amber and coins from Roman Aquileia.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-arcevia.name: National Archaeological Museum of Arcevia
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-arcevia.description: National archaeological museum opened in 1996 in Arcevia's former Franciscan convent, whose church of San Francesco was built in 1275 and remodelled in Baroque style in 1750. The collection ranges from Palaeolithic flint tools found at Ponte di Pietra to Gallic burial assemblages from the Montefortino necropolis.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-ascoli-p.name: National Archaeological Museum of Ascoli Piceno
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-ascoli-p.description: National archaeological museum established in 1981 from the town's Civic Archaeological Collection, housed in the 16th-century Palazzo Panichi. It documents the Piceni culture of the Tronto, Tesino and Salino valleys through to the Roman period, with a mosaic showing a double-faced herm and a portrait of Trajan among its Roman holdings.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-cagliari.name: National Archaeological Museum of Cagliari
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-cagliari.description: The most important archaeological museum in Sardinia, founded in 1800 as a cabinet of archaeology and natural history under Viceroy Carlo Felice and opened to the public in 1802. Since 1993 it has occupied the Cittadella dei Musei, designed by architects Piero Gazzola and Libero Cecchini, displaying Sardinian finds from prehistory to the Byzantine period across four floors.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-calatia.name: National Archaeological Museum of Calatia
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-calatia.description: National archaeological museum inaugurated in 2003 to display finds from the ancient city of Calatia, dating from the 8th century BC onward. It occupies the Casino di Starza Penta, a 16th-century fortified farmhouse of the Carafa della Stadera family that also hosted the Bourbon king Charles III on hunting trips, its five rooms arranged around a courtyard with a reconstructed Roman house.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-campli.name: National Archaeological Museum of Campli
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-campli.description: National archaeological museum inaugurated in 1988 in rooms of the San Francesco convent in Campli, dedicated to the nearby Campovalano necropolis. Its display of some 610 burials from the 9th to 3rd centuries BC includes funerary tumuli, bronze weapons, chariots, amber jewellery, ivory plaques and glass-paste ornaments.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-canosa-d.name: National Archaeological Museum of Canosa di Puglia
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-canosa-d.description: State archaeology museum in Canosa di Puglia, Apulia, devoted to ancient Canusium, a Daunian and later Roman city known for its extensive necropolises. It displays finds recovered from excavations in the local area.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-cingoli-.name: National Archaeological Museum of Cingoli
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-cingoli-.description: National archaeological museum opened in 1994 and expanded in 1997, housed in Cingoli's Palazzo Comunale. Its four sections trace the area from some of the Marche region's oldest Palaeolithic stone tools through Bronze Age finds from the Moscosi site and material from a 6th-century BC sanctuary at San Vittore, to Roman ceramics, bronzes and coins.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-cividale.name: National Archaeological Museum of Cividale del Friuli
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-cividale.description: National archaeological museum founded in 1817 by Count Michele Della Torre di Valsassina to establish Cividale as the site of the Roman municipium of Forum Iulii. Since 1990 it has occupied the Palazzo dei Provveditori Veneti, a 16th-century building traditionally attributed to Andrea Palladio, and its collection centres on Lombard funerary archaeology alongside Roman inscriptions and bronzes from Zuglio.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-civitave.name: National Archaeological Museum of Civitavecchia
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-civitave.description: National archaeological museum housed in an 18th-century palace built under Pope Clement XIII as headquarters for the papal garrison. Across three floors it displays finds from the Roman port city of Centumcellae and the nearby Monte Rovello archaeological site.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-eboli.name: National Archaeological Museum of Eboli and the Middle Sele Valley
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-eboli.description: National archaeological museum opened in 2000 in the former Convent of San Francesco, founded in the 13th century and remodelled in the 16th and 18th, which served as Eboli's town hall and courthouse before wartime bombing led to its abandonment and 1990s restoration. Its 600 square metres of galleries display pottery, weapons, jewellery and funerary goods from the Neolithic to the Middle Ages found across the middle Sele Valley.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-ferrara.name: National Archaeological Museum of Ferrara
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-ferrara.description: National archaeological museum opened in 1935 in Palazzo Costabili to house finds from Spina, the Etruscan port city that flourished from the 6th to the 3rd century BC and yielded more than 4,000 excavated tombs. The collection includes Athenian red-figure pottery, Etruscan bronzes and gold, silver and amber jewellery.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-firenze.name: National Archaeological Museum of Florence
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-firenze.description: National museum of classical, Etruscan and Egyptian antiquities, first opened in 1870 and moved in 1880 to the Palazzo della Crocetta, built between 1619 and 1621 by architect Giulio Parigi for Princess Maria Maddalena de' Medici. Its holdings include the Chimera of Arezzo, the bronze Orator (Arringatore) and the François Vase, alongside one of Italy's major Egyptian collections.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-formia.name: National Archaeological Museum of Formia
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-formia.description: National archaeological museum established in 1968 and installed in its present galleries in 1997, on the ground floor of the Palazzo Municipale in rooms known as the 'Stalloni dei Borbone.' It displays Roman imperial sculpture, portraits, funerary monuments and frescoes from Formia's forum area and the maritime villa at Gianola.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-fratta-p.name: National Archaeological Museum of Fratta Polesine
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-fratta-p.description: State archaeology museum opened in 2009 in the north barchessa of Villa Badoer, a villa designed by Andrea Palladio in 1554-55 and built in 1556-63 for Francesco Badoer, part of the UNESCO-listed Palladian villas of the Veneto. It presents Late Bronze Age finds from the nearby settlement of Frattesina and its cemeteries at Narde and Fondo Zanotto, including gold and glass objects, bronze weapons, and cremation urns from around a thousand burials.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-mattinat.name: "Matteo Sansone" National Archaeological Museum of Mattinata
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-mattinat.description: State archaeology museum in Mattinata, on the Gargano promontory in Apulia, named after local archaeologist and collector Matteo Sansone. It displays archaeological finds recovered in the surrounding area.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-napoli.name: National Archaeological Museum of Naples
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-napoli.description: One of the world's foremost archaeological museums, founded in 1777 by Ferdinand IV and opened in 1816 as the Real Museo Borbonico in the Palazzo degli Studi, remodelled from a university building by architect Ferdinando Fuga. It unites the Farnese collection of ancient sculpture, including the Farnese Bull, with finds from Pompeii, Herculaneum and Stabiae, an Egyptian collection, and mosaics, frescoes and a numismatic collection of more than 150,000 coins.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-orvieto.name: National Archaeological Museum of Orvieto
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-orvieto.description: National archaeological museum housed in the late-13th-century Palazzo Papale in Orvieto, displaying mainly Etruscan ceramics, bronzes and jewellery from the local necropolises of Crocifisso del Tufo and Cannicella, alongside reconstructed copies of the painted Golini tombs.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-pontecag.name: National Archaeological Museum and Archaeological Park of Pontecagnano
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-pontecag.description: National archaeological museum and adjoining park opened in 2007, built on systematic excavations begun in 1962 by archaeologist Bruno D'Agostino at the Villanovan-then-Etruscan settlement of Pontecagnano. Its exhibition, 'Gli Etruschi di frontiera' (Etruscans of the Frontier), draws on some 9,000 excavated tombs to trace Etruscan expansion into southern Italy from around 3000 to the 3rd century BC.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-sala-con.name: National Archaeological Museum of Sala Consilina
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-sala-con.description: State archaeology museum in Sala Consilina, in the Vallo di Diano area of Campania, presenting pre-Roman finds from necropolises in the surrounding territory.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-sessa-au.name: National Archaeological Museum of Sessa Aurunca
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-sessa-au.description: National archaeological museum inaugurated in December 2024, the first dedicated archaeological museum in Sessa Aurunca's history. Housed in the Norman-era Castello Ducale, built over earlier Lombard and Roman structures, it presents the pre-Roman Ausoni and Aurunci peoples, the sanctuary of the goddess Marica on the Garigliano river, and Roman Suessa, including its theatre, with the Venus of Sinuessa on loan from the Naples archaeological museum.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-sperlong.name: National Archaeological Museum of Sperlonga and Archaeological Area
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-sperlong.description: National archaeological museum built specifically to house the monumental sculptural groups recovered in fragments during the late 1950s from a seaside grotto within Emperor Tiberius's villa at Sperlonga. The four groups, 1st-century AD Roman versions of Greek originals of the 5th-2nd centuries BC, depict episodes from Homer's Odyssey, including the blinding of Polyphemus.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-taranto-.name: National Archaeological Museum of Taranto (MArTA)
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-taranto-.description: National archaeological museum founded in 1887 and housed in the former 18th-century convent of San Pasquale di Baylon, holding one of the largest collections of Magna Graecia material, including the celebrated 'Ori di Taranto' gold jewellery. A major renovation between 2000 and 2007 was followed by the 2016 reopening of the second floor and, in 2023, the return of the Orpheus and Sirens sculptural group after fifty years abroad.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-teanum-s.name: National Archaeological Museum of Teanum Sidicinum
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-teanum-s.description: National archaeological museum of ancient Teanum Sidicinum, housed in the 14th-century late-Gothic 'Loggione e Cavallerizza' complex once owned by the Marzano family. Its seven rooms display material spanning the Middle Palaeolithic to the 7th century AD, including a mosaic bearing the earliest known depiction of the Epiphany, dated to around 375 AD.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-tuscania.name: National Archaeological Museum of Tuscania
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-tuscania.description: National archaeological museum housed in a former Franciscan convent beside the church of Santa Maria del Riposo in Tuscania, displaying Etruscan finds from the town's necropolises, notably from the tombs of the Curunas and Vipinas families.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-venafro.name: National Archaeological Museum of Venafro
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-venafro.description: National archaeological museum established in 1931 to display finds made about a decade earlier near Monte Santa Croce, reopened in the 1970s in the former convent of Santa Chiara donated by the municipality. Its collection spans the Samnite period of the 6th-4th centuries BC through the Roman and early medieval eras, including the 2nd-century AD statue known as the Venus of Venafro.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-venezia.name: National Archaeological Museum of Venice
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-venezia.description: National archaeological museum built on antiquities bequeathed to the Republic of Venice by Cardinal Domenico Grimani in 1523 and expanded by his nephew Giovanni Grimani from 1563, forming the public statuary ('Statuario pubblico') formalised in 1596. Housed in the Procuratie Nuove on Piazza San Marco, it holds Greek sculpture, Roman portraits and reliefs, gems, coins and Egyptian and Assyro-Babylonian antiquities.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-verona.name: National Archaeological Museum of Verona
museo-archeologico-nazionale-di-verona.description: National archaeological museum opened in 2022 in a former Austrian military prison built in neo-medieval style on the site of a 13th-16th-century Carmelite monastery. It displays prehistoric and protohistoric material from the Verona area, including a painted stone from Fumane Cave dated to around 38,000 years ago, described as the oldest surviving European Upper Palaeolithic pictorial representation.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-e-castello-.name: National Archaeological Museum and Castle of Gioia del Colle
museo-archeologico-nazionale-e-castello-.description: State archaeology museum on the ground floor of the Norman-Swabian castle of Gioia del Colle, a stronghold of 9th-century Byzantine origin enlarged by the Norman lord Riccardo Siniscalco in the 12th century and given its present form by Frederick II around 1230. Founded in 1959 and raised to national status in 1977, the museum presents Peucetian and Iron Age material from excavations at Monte Sannace and Santo Mola conducted between 1940 and 1953.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-e-parco-arc.name: National Archaeological Museum and Archaeological Park of Cosa
museo-archeologico-nazionale-e-parco-arc.description: State museum and archaeological park at Cosa, a Latin colony founded around 273 BC on a hilltop above the Tyrrhenian coast near Orbetello, excavated from 1948 by the American Academy in Rome. Opened in 1981, the museum stands within the colony's walls over the Casa del Tesoro and displays ceramics, sculpture, coins from Cosa's own mint, inscriptions, and finds from the town's port and necropolis.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-e-parco-arc.name: National Archaeological Museum and Park of Urbs Salvia
museo-archeologico-nazionale-e-parco-arc.description: Archaeological park covering some 40 hectares of the Roman city of Urbs Salvia, founded as the colony of Pollentia in the mid-2nd century BC and renamed under Augustus, with one of Italy's largest Roman theatres, an amphitheatre, a temple complex and city walls. Its museum, drawing on excavations under way since 1995, displays finds from the site and its surrounding territory.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-e-teatro-ro.name: National Archaeological Museum and Roman Theatre of Spoleto
museo-archeologico-nazionale-e-teatro-ro.description: National archaeological museum opened in 1985 within the former Benedictine monastery of Sant'Agata, founded in 1396 over the 11th-century Palazzo Corvi, itself built above the remains of Spoleto's Roman theatre. Excavation of the theatre began in 1933 and resumed in 1954 after wartime interruption, and the museum's collection spans the 4th millennium BC to the 4th century AD.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-gaio-cilnio.name: "Gaio Cilnio Mecenate" National Archaeological Museum
museo-archeologico-nazionale-gaio-cilnio.description: Archaeological museum in Arezzo housed in a former Olivetan monastery beside the remains of the city's Roman amphitheatre, named after Gaius Maecenas, the Augustan-age patron of the arts who was born in ancient Arretium. Its collection is renowned for Aretine terra sigillata, the fine red-gloss pottery produced in the city in the first century BCE.

museo-archeologico-nazionale-giuseppe-an.name: "Giuseppe Andreassi" National Archaeological Museum and Archaeological Park of Egnazia
museo-archeologico-nazionale-giuseppe-an.description: Museum built in 1978 beside the excavations of Egnazia, an ancient Messapian settlement north of Fasano that flourished as a Roman port on the Via Traiana before declining after the Gothic Wars in the sixth century. Its collection includes Messapian tomb goods, Gnathia-ware pottery and objects linked to the cult of Cybele.

museo-archeologico-statale-di-castiglion.name: State Archaeological Museum of Castiglioncello
museo-archeologico-statale-di-castiglion.description: State archaeological museum founded in 1914 by archaeologist Luigi Adriano Milani, one of Italy's earliest decentralized museums, closed in 1972 when its collection moved to Florence and reopened in 2011. Its hilltop building, designed with forms evoking Etruscan temples and cinerary urns, displays material from an Etruscan necropolis of the 4th-1st centuries BC uncovered during construction work between 1903 and 1911.

museo-casa-natale-di-gabriele-d-annunzio.name: Gabriele D'Annunzio Birthplace Museum
museo-casa-natale-di-gabriele-d-annunzio.description: House museum in the 18th-century building where the writer Gabriele D'Annunzio was born, owned by his family from the early 19th century and declared a national monument in 1927. Restored under state ownership after 1933 and reopened following wartime bomb damage, it has displayed the poet's furnishings and personal effects across nine first-floor rooms since 1963.

museo-civico-e-della-ceramica-di-ariano-.name: Civic Museum and Ceramics Museum of Ariano Irpino
museo-civico-e-della-ceramica-di-ariano-.description: Civic museum in Ariano Irpino's Palazzo Forte, combining rare 16th-17th century printed books from suppressed convents and a civic photographic archive with a ceramics collection spanning the 12th to 21st centuries, particularly the town's own production of the 17th-18th centuries, whose local ceramic tradition is documented from the early 14th century onward. A separate didactic wing in Palazzo San Giacomo occupies the historic kiln district of Tranesi.

museo-d-arte-orientale-venezia.name: Museum of Oriental Art, Venice
museo-d-arte-orientale-venezia.description: Museum of Asian art established in 1928, occupying the third floor of Ca' Pesaro on the Grand Canal. Its holdings, formed around more than 30,000 objects Prince Henry of Bourbon-Parma acquired during travels in 1887-1889, include one of Europe's major collections of Japanese Edo-period art alongside Chinese jade and porcelain and Indonesian textiles and shadow puppets.

museo-delle-civilta.name: Museum of Civilisations
museo-delle-civilta.description: State museum created in 2016 by consolidating six former national museums, spanning art, ethnology, anthropology and paleontology from prehistory to the present. It occupies two rationalist buildings in Rome's EUR district, designed for the Universal Exposition planned for 1942 but never held, housing African, American, Asian and Oceanic collections alongside early medieval and colonial-era material.

museo-delle-navi-antiche.name: Museum of Ancient Ships, Pisa
museo-delle-navi-antiche.description: Archaeological museum opened in 2019 to display ancient ships discovered in 1998 during construction work at Pisa's San Rossore station, where nine catastrophic floods over twelve centuries had buried around thirty vessels dating from the 2nd century BC to the 7th century AD, together with more than 13,000 amphorae. It occupies the Arsenali Medicei, historic shipyards built for the galleys of the Knights of Santo Stefano.

museo-delle-arti-e-tradizioni-popolari-d.name: Museum of Arts and Folk Traditions of the Upper Tiber Valley - Palazzo Taglieschi
museo-delle-arti-e-tradizioni-popolari-d.description: Museum of sacred art and folk traditions of the upper Tiber valley, inaugurated in 1975 around a 1959 bequest from the priest and collector Don Nilo Conti. It occupies Palazzo Taglieschi in Anghiari, a medieval tower-house complex remodelled in Renaissance style in 1437, and displays religious works from the 14th to 18th centuries, including a polychrome wooden Madonna and Child attributed to Jacopo della Quercia, alongside domestic and agricultural objects of local folk life.

museo-di-casa-giusti.name: Casa Giusti Museum
museo-di-casa-giusti.description: House museum in the 17th-century Giusti family home, enlarged between 1791 and 1793, where the poet Giuseppe Giusti was born in 1809. Acquired by the state in 1972 and opened as a national museum in 1992, it preserves early-19th-century furnishings and artworks, including a portrait of the poet by Giuseppe Bezzuoli, alongside a documentary section on his work.

museo-di-casa-vasari.name: Casa Vasari Museum
museo-di-casa-vasari.description: House museum in the residence Giorgio Vasari bought in 1541 and decorated with frescoes between 1542 and 1568, acquired by the Italian state in 1911. Alongside some sixty paintings from Florentine gallery collections, it preserves the Vasarian Archive, including seventeen autograph letters from Michelangelo with three sonnets and drawings.

museo-di-palazzo-ducale-di-mantova.name: Ducal Palace of Mantua
museo-di-palazzo-ducale-di-mantova.description: Former residence of the rulers of Mantua from 1308, first the Bonacolsi and then the Gonzaga dynasty, opened as a museum in 1887. Built up over four centuries and unified under architect Giovan Battista Bertani around 1556, its more than 500 rooms include Andrea Mantegna's Camera degli Sposi (1465-74), Pisanello's Arthurian fresco cycle and Isabella d'Este's studiolo.

museo-di-palazzo-grimani.name: Palazzo Grimani Museum
museo-di-palazzo-grimani.description: Renaissance palace near Santa Maria Formosa in Venice, remodeled from the 1530s to the 1560s for the Procurator Vettore Grimani and the Patriarch Giovanni Grimani, with a monumental staircase frescoed by Federico Zuccari and rooms decorated by Francesco Salviati, Giovanni da Udine, and Camillo Mantovano. Giovanni Grimani's antiquities collection, once displayed in the palace's Tribuna, passed to the Republic of Venice in 1587 and formed the core of the city's Archaeological Museum; the state acquired the palace in 1981 and reopened it as a museum in 2008.

museo-di-palazzo-nieddu-del-rio.name: Museum of Palazzo Nieddu del Rio
museo-di-palazzo-nieddu-del-rio.description: National archaeological museum in Locri, in the historic Palazzo Nieddu del Rio on Corso Vittorio Emanuele. It is a small institution operated by Italy's Ministry of Culture, in a town best known for the nearby Greek colony of Locri Epizefiri.

museo-di-san-marco.name: Museum of San Marco
museo-di-san-marco.description: State museum in the former Dominican convent of San Marco, rebuilt for Cosimo de' Medici by architect Michelozzo between 1439 and 1444 and opened as a museum in 1869. It preserves the largest collection of works by Fra Angelico, including 44 frescoed monastic cells, alongside paintings by Fra Bartolomeo and Mariotto Albertinelli and a library of 115 illuminated manuscripts.

museo-e-parco-archeologico-dell-antica-k.name: Archaeological Museum and Park of Ancient Kaulonia
museo-e-parco-archeologico-dell-antica-k.description: Archaeological park and museum on the Ionian coast of Calabria preserving the remains of Kaulonia, a Greek colony founded by Achaean settlers, probably from Croton, in the 7th century BC and destroyed by Dionysius I of Syracuse in 389 BC. The site includes the foundations of a Doric temple and stretches of the city walls, while the museum displays coins, ceramics and finds from recent excavations.

museo-e-parco-archeologico-di-bova-marin.name: Archeoderi Museum and Archaeological Park
museo-e-parco-archeologico-di-bova-marin.description: Museum and archaeological park in Bova Marina, Calabria, built around the remains of a synagogue dating from the 4th to the 6th century AD, discovered by chance in 1986 and among the oldest known in Italy after Ostia Antica. The site preserves a 30-square-metre mosaic floor decorated with a menorah, shofar, etrog, and palm branch, the principal evidence of a Jewish community in Roman-era Calabria.

museo-e-parco-archeologico-nazionale-di-.name: Locri Epizephyrii National Archaeological Museum and Park
museo-e-parco-archeologico-nazionale-di-.description: Archaeological museum and park at Locri Epizefiri, a Greek colony founded around 680 BC by settlers from Locris in mainland Greece, one of the major cities of Magna Graecia on Calabria's Ionian coast. Excavations have uncovered the Doric temple of Marasà, a theatre and the sanctuary of Persephone, and the museum houses the site's celebrated terracotta pinakes, votive plaques depicting the goddess.

museo-e-parco-archeologico-nazionale-di-.name: Scolacium National Archaeological Museum and Park
museo-e-parco-archeologico-nazionale-di-.description: Archaeological park on the site of Scolacium, a Roman colony established under Gaius Gracchus in the late 2nd century BC and further developed under the emperor Nerva, on the Ionian coast near Catanzaro. Set among olive groves, it preserves the forum, a theatre seating around 5,000 spectators and Calabria's only known Roman amphitheatre, alongside the Norman-era ruins of the Santa Maria della Roccella church.

museo-e-real-bosco-di-capodimonte.name: Capodimonte Museum and Royal Park
museo-e-real-bosco-di-capodimonte.description: Museum and park in Naples occupying the royal palace begun in 1738 for Charles of Bourbon to house the Farnese art collection he inherited from his mother, Elisabetta Farnese. Its galleries hold masterpieces including Titian's Danaë and Caravaggio's Flagellation of Christ, and the surrounding Real Bosco park was laid out as a royal hunting reserve.

museo-in-palazzo-pistilli.name: Palazzo Pistilli Museum
museo-in-palazzo-pistilli.description: Art museum in Campobasso housed in a noble residence built towards the end of the 18th century, the city's only state-run art museum. It displays the collection assembled over five decades by Michele Praitano and donated to the state in 2014, focused on 18th- to 20th-century painting, alongside works from the Eliseo family collections.

museo-nazionale-memoriale-giuseppe-garib.name: Giuseppe Garibaldi National Memorial Museum
museo-nazionale-memoriale-giuseppe-garib.description: Memorial museum on the island of Caprera, near La Maddalena, preserving the house where Giuseppe Garibaldi settled in 1856 and died in 1882. Known as the Compendio Garibaldino, it retains his residence, the Casa Bianca, together with his personal belongings, weapons and the family cemetery where he is buried, and has been open as a museum since 1978.

museo-nazionale-atestino.name: Atestino National Museum
museo-nazionale-atestino.description: Archaeological museum in Este housed in the 16th-century Palazzo Mocenigo, named after the pre-Roman Veneti settlement of Ateste. Founded in 1880, it holds one of the principal collections of the ancient Este civilization, including situla art bronzes and grave goods from the Iron Age necropolises, alongside later Roman-era finds.

museo-nazionale-collezione-salce-sede-di.name: Salce Collection National Museum, San Gaetano
museo-nazionale-collezione-salce-sede-di.description: Poster museum in Treviso housed in the former church complex of San Gaetano, home to the collection bequeathed to the Italian state in 1962 by the local collector Ferdinando Salce, who had assembled some 25,000 posters over seven decades. Now numbering around 50,000 pieces, the collection spans a century of Italian graphic design, with works by Marcello Dudovich, Leonetto Cappiello and Fortunato Depero.

museo-nazionale-collezione-salce-sede-di.name: Salce Collection National Museum, Santa Margherita venue
museo-nazionale-collezione-salce-sede-di.description: National museum in the former 13th-century church of Santa Margherita in Treviso, opened in 2021, housing the poster collection assembled between 1895 and his death in 1962 by local collector Ferdinando Salce and bequeathed by him to the Italian state. The roughly 50,000-piece collection spans the late 19th to the mid-20th century and includes work by Marcello Dudovich, Leonetto Cappiello, and Leopoldo Metlicovitz.

museo-nazionale-jatta.name: Jatta National Museum
museo-nazionale-jatta.description: Archaeological museum in Ruvo di Puglia built around a collection begun in the early 19th century by the magistrate Giovanni Jatta and expanded by his nephew, before its acquisition by the Italian state in 1991. It holds around 2,500 pieces, mostly Greek and locally made red-figure vases, including the 5th-century BC Talos krater depicting the death of the bronze giant Talos.

museo-nazionale-archeologico-e-castello-.name: Manfredonia National Archaeological Museum and Castle
museo-nazionale-archeologico-e-castello-.description: Castle and archaeological museum in Manfredonia, begun in 1279 under Charles I of Anjou and enlarged by the Aragonese around 1442 with cylindrical corner towers. Since 1968 it has housed the Museo Archeologico Nazionale, known above all for its collection of Daunian stelae, carved limestone slabs from the Iron Age necropolises of the Gargano and Tavoliere.

museo-nazionale-archeologico-ed-etnograf.name: Giovanni Antonio Sanna National Archaeological and Ethnographic Museum
museo-nazionale-archeologico-ed-etnograf.description: Archaeological and ethnographic museum in Sassari named after the mining entrepreneur Giovanni Antonio Sanna, whose bequest funded its foundation. Sardinia's second-largest archaeological museum after Cagliari, it holds prehistoric Nuragic material and Phoenician, Punic and Roman finds from the island's north, alongside an ethnographic section on traditional Sardinian life.

museo-nazionale-d-arte-medievale-e-moder.name: National Museum of Medieval and Modern Art, Arezzo
museo-nazionale-d-arte-medievale-e-moder.description: Museum in Arezzo occupying the mid-15th-century Palazzo Bruni-Ciocchi, built for Donato Bruni with a courtyard attributed to Bernardo Rossellino. Its galleries trace art from the early Middle Ages to the 19th century, with gold-ground panels by Margarito d'Arezzo, frescoes by Spinello Aretino and works by Luca Signorelli and Giorgio Vasari, alongside one of Italy's richest collections of Renaissance maiolica.

museo-nazionale-degli-strumenti-musicali.name: National Museum of Musical Instruments
museo-nazionale-degli-strumenti-musicali.description: Museum in Rome devoted to the history of musical instruments, built around the collection assembled by tenor Evan Gorga in the early 20th century. Highlights include the monumental Barberini harp and one of the earliest surviving pianos, built around 1722 by Bartolomeo Cristofori, the instrument's Florentine inventor.

museo-nazionale-del-paleolitico-di-isern.name: Isernia National Paleolithic Museum
museo-nazionale-del-paleolitico-di-isern.description: Museum in Isernia dedicated to the Paleolithic site of La Pineta, discovered in 1979 during highway works and dated to around 600,000-700,000 years ago, among the oldest evidence of human presence in Europe. The site preserved a butchering ground littered with animal bones and stone tools, now presented alongside the excavation itself.

museo-nazionale-delle-residenze-napoleon.name: National Museum of the Napoleonic Residences – Villa San Martino
museo-nazionale-delle-residenze-napoleon.description: Napoleon's country residence on Elba, built below Portoferraio and occupied during his exile from May 1814 to February 1815, while the nearby Palazzina dei Mulini handled his official duties. In 1851 Prince Anatoly Demidoff, who had married Napoleon's niece Mathilde Bonaparte, added the neoclassical Demidoff Gallery designed by Niccolò Matas and inaugurated in 1859, now displaying Napoleonic memorabilia, paintings and sculpture, including a Galatea attributed to Canova.

museo-nazionale-di-castello-pandone.name: Castello Pandone National Museum
museo-nazionale-di-castello-pandone.description: Castle in Venafro with a megalithic core, developed under the Normans and Angevins before passing to the Pandone family in 1443. Count Enrico Pandone had the noble apartments frescoed with life-size portraits of his prized stallions, each bearing his monogram and an inscription naming the horse, its breed and the nobleman it was destined for, one having been a gift to Emperor Charles V.

museo-nazionale-di-mileto.name: National Museum of Mileto
museo-nazionale-di-mileto.description: State museum in Mileto, the Calabrian town made his capital by the Norman count Roger I de Hauteville in the 11th century and levelled by the earthquake of 1783. Its holdings gather architectural and sculptural fragments rescued from the destroyed town, including material from the Norman abbey of Santissima Trinità, founded by Roger I and his burial place.

museo-nazionale-di-palazzo-reale.name: Palazzo Reale National Museum, Pisa
museo-nazionale-di-palazzo-reale.description: Museum in Pisa housed in the Palazzo Reale, remodelled in the mid-16th century as a residence for Cosimo I de' Medici and later used by the House of Savoy. Its rooms display Medici and Savoy portraits, arms and armour, tapestries and decorative arts collected across the palace's history as a royal residence.

museo-nazionale-di-ravenna.name: National Museum of Ravenna
museo-nazionale-di-ravenna.description: Museum in Ravenna occupying the cloisters of the former Camaldolese monastery adjoining the Basilica of San Vitale. Its collections trace the city's Roman and Byzantine past through ivories, textiles, icons, ceramics and archaeological finds, including material from the city's early Christian monuments.

museo-nazionale-di-san-matteo.name: National Museum of San Matteo, Pisa
museo-nazionale-di-san-matteo.description: Museum in Pisa housed in the former Benedictine convent of San Matteo, gathering the city's medieval and Renaissance sculpture and painting. Highlights include works by Giovanni Pisano, Donatello's reliquary bust of San Rossore and a polyptych by Simone Martini.

museo-nazionale-di-villa-guinigi.name: Villa Guinigi National Museum
museo-nazionale-di-villa-guinigi.description: Museum in Lucca housed in the Villa Guinigi, built in the early 15th century for Paolo Guinigi, lord of the city. It brings together Lucca's archaeological finds with medieval and Renaissance sculpture and painting, including works by the local sculptor Matteo Civitali and by Fra Bartolomeo.

museo-nazionale-di-archeologia-del-mare.name: National Museum of Maritime Archaeology, Caorle
museo-nazionale-di-archeologia-del-mare.description: Museum in Caorle occupying early 20th-century buildings of the former Chiggiato farm estate, opened in 2014 after restoration. Its collection ranges from Late Bronze Age artefacts found around the lagoon to the history of the brig Mercurio, a Napoleonic-era warship that exploded during the 1812 Battle of Grado.

museo-nazionale-di-archeologia-subacquea.name: National Museum of Underwater Archaeology of the Upper Adriatic
museo-nazionale-di-archeologia-subacquea.description: National museum in Grado, opened in December 2025 to house the Iulia Felix, a Roman merchant ship of the 3rd century AD discovered in 1986 and recovered from the seabed in 1999. The 18-metre vessel carried around 560 amphorae of preserved fish along with glass and bronze objects, including statuettes of Poseidon and Minerva, bound for nearby Aquileia.

museo-nazionale-e-parco-archeologico-di-.name: National Museum and Archaeological Park of Luni
museo-nazionale-e-parco-archeologico-di-.description: Museum and open-air site on the ruins of Luna, the Roman colony founded on the Tyrrhenian coast in 177 BC and long prosperous through the marble trade from the nearby Apuan quarries. Established in 1964, the museum stands amid the excavations and displays sculpture, mosaics, coins and household objects from the town, whose visible remains include the forum, an amphitheatre and a theatre.

museo-nazionale-etrusco-pompeo-aria-e-pa.name: Pompeo Aria National Etruscan Museum and Kainua Archaeological Park
museo-nazionale-etrusco-pompeo-aria-e-pa.description: Archaeological park and museum at Marzabotto preserving Kainua, an Etruscan city laid out on a regular grid plan in the late 6th century BC, with paved streets, a drainage system and temples on its acropolis. The museum, named after the archaeologist Pompeo Aria who led the excavations, displays finds from the city and its necropolises.

museo-nazionale-etrusco-di-rocca-alborno.name: Rocca Albornoz National Etruscan Museum
museo-nazionale-etrusco-di-rocca-alborno.description: Museum in Viterbo housed in the Rocca Albornoz, a fortress built in 1354 for Cardinal Egidio Albornoz and later remodelled under Pope Julius II with a courtyard attributed to Bramante. Opened in 1986 after postwar restoration, it displays Etruscan finds from northern Lazio, including a bronze chariot from Ischia di Castro and architectural terracottas from the settlement of Acquarossa.

museo-nazionale-etrusco-di-villa-giulia.name: Villa Giulia National Etruscan Museum
museo-nazionale-etrusco-di-villa-giulia.description: National Etruscan museum in Rome housed in the Villa Giulia, built in 1551-1553 as a suburban retreat for Pope Julius III. Its collection, drawn largely from the necropolises of southern Etruria, includes the terracotta Sarcophagus of the Spouses from Cerveteri and the gold Pyrgi Tablets bearing a bilingual Etruscan-Phoenician inscription.

museo-nazionale-etrusco-necropoli-di-pog.name: National Etruscan Museum – Poggio Renzo Necropolis and Tomba del Colle
museo-nazionale-etrusco-necropoli-di-pog.description: Archaeological museum in Chiusi devoted to the Etruscan city of Clusium, founded as a municipal collection in 1871, rehoused in its present neoclassical building in 1901 and taken over by the state in 1963. Its holdings, arranged from the Bronze Age to the Roman period, include Etruscan cinerary urns, notably the anthropomorphic Dolciano canopic urn, imported Attic pottery, and finds from the surrounding necropolises, among them Poggio Renzo and the Tomba del Colle.

museo-nazionale-romano-palazzo-altemps.name: National Roman Museum - Palazzo Altemps
museo-nazionale-romano-palazzo-altemps.description: One of the four venues of the Museo Nazionale Romano, occupying the Renaissance Palazzo Altemps near Piazza Navona. Its rooms display the Ludovisi collection of classical sculpture, assembled in the 17th century, including the celebrated Ludovisi Throne.

museo-nazionale-romano-palazzo-massimo.name: National Roman Museum - Palazzo Massimo
museo-nazionale-romano-palazzo-massimo.description: One of the four venues of the Museo Nazionale Romano, near Rome's Termini station. It houses Roman sculpture and mosaics of the Republican and Imperial periods, including the bronze Boxer at Rest and the frescoed garden room from the Villa of Livia.

museo-nazionale-romano-terme-di-dioclezi.name: National Roman Museum - Baths of Diocletian
museo-nazionale-romano-terme-di-dioclezi.description: One of the four venues of the Museo Nazionale Romano, set within the vast ruins of the Baths of Diocletian, completed in 306 AD. It houses the museum's epigraphic collection, one of the largest of its kind, along with material documenting the prehistory and protohistory of Latium.

museo-paleontologico-luigi-boldrini-di-p.name: Luigi Boldrini Paleontological Museum of Pietrafitta
museo-paleontologico-luigi-boldrini-di-p.description: Paleontological museum in Piegaro named after Luigi Boldrini, a mine worker who began recovering fossils in the 1940s from a lignite quarry in the Nestore valley. The collection consists of Lower Pleistocene vertebrate remains, including the elephant Mammuthus meridionalis and several rhinoceros species, and the site became a state museum in 2023.

museo-preistorico-dei-balzi-rossi-e-zona.name: Balzi Rossi Prehistoric Museum and Archaeological Area
museo-preistorico-dei-balzi-rossi-e-zona.description: Prehistoric museum and archaeological area at Ventimiglia, on a cluster of caves near the French border explored since the 19th century. Excavations from the Upper Paleolithic yielded human burials, known as the Grimaldi Men, and a group of small carved female figurines, the Balzi Rossi Venuses, now displayed alongside the site.

museo-storico-archeologico-di-nola-e-are.name: Historical-Archaeological Museum of Nola and Archaeological Area of San Paolo Belsito
museo-storico-archeologico-di-nola-e-are.description: Museum in Nola housed since 2000 in the former Santa Maria la Nova convent complex, tracing the area's history from prehistory to the medieval period. Its collection includes remains of the Copper Age hut village of Nola-Croce del Papa, Etruscan and Greek grave goods, Roman material from the Villa Augustea at Somma Vesuviana, and, at the associated site of San Paolo Belsito, further evidence of ancient settlement in the Nolan plain.

museo-storico-della-liberazione.name: Historical Museum of the Liberation
museo-storico-della-liberazione.description: Museum in Rome housed in the building on Via Tasso used by the German security police as a prison and interrogation site during the Nazi occupation of the city in 1943-1944. Cells bearing prisoners' inscriptions have been preserved, and the museum documents the Italian Resistance and the deportations of the period.

museo-storico-e-parco-del-castello-di-mi.name: Miramare Castle Historical Museum and Park
museo-storico-e-parco-del-castello-di-mi.description: Castle and park on the Gulf of Trieste, built between 1856 and 1860 for Archduke Maximilian of Habsburg, later Emperor of Mexico, and his wife Charlotte of Belgium. The museum preserves the couple's original 19th-century apartments, while the surrounding park combines formal and English-style gardens with rare botanical species.

necropoli-romana-di-voghenza.name: Voghenza Roman Necropolis
necropoli-romana-di-voghenza.description: Roman necropolis at Voghenza, near Ferrara, marking the site of Vicus Habentia, probably the earliest Roman settlement in the area. Burial enclosures and stone sarcophagi from the 1st to 3rd centuries AD remain visible in situ, while grave goods including glass, amber and gold ornaments are displayed at the nearby Belriguardo museum.

necropoli-etrusca-di-crocifisso-del-tufo.name: Crocifisso del Tufo Etruscan Necropolis
necropoli-etrusca-di-crocifisso-del-tufo.description: Etruscan necropolis on the outskirts of Orvieto, in use from the 6th century BC, where cube-shaped tombs are laid out along a regular grid of streets. Each tomb bears the name of its occupant carved above the doorway, offering a rare record of the city's Etruscan inhabitants.

palazzo-altieri.name: Palazzo Altieri, Oriolo Romano
palazzo-altieri.description: Renaissance palace in Oriolo Romano, built between 1579 and 1585 for Giorgio Santacroce, founder of the town, and passed to the Orsini and then, from 1671, the Altieri family, who enlarged it with the architect Carlo Fontana after Emilio Altieri's election as Pope Clement X. Its frescoed rooms include a gallery of papal portraits, and it has been open as a state museum since 2014.

palazzo-besta.name: Palazzo Besta
palazzo-besta.description: Renaissance palace in Teglio, in the Valtellina, built in the mid-16th century for the noble Besta family. Its rooms are decorated with mythological frescoes and it retains an elegant loggiato courtyard typical of Lombard Renaissance architecture.

palazzo-ducale-di-gubbio.name: Ducal Palace of Gubbio
palazzo-ducale-di-gubbio.description: Renaissance palace in Gubbio built in the 1470s for Federico da Montefeltro, Duke of Urbino, as a smaller counterpart to his palace in Urbino. Its studiolo, a small study once lined with inlaid wood panels of illusionistic scenes, was dismantled and is now held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York.

palazzo-ducale-di-urbino-galleria-nazion.name: Ducal Palace of Urbino – National Gallery of the Marche
palazzo-ducale-di-urbino-galleria-nazion.description: Renaissance palace built largely for Duke Federico da Montefeltro by architects Luciano Laurana and Francesco di Giorgio Martini, notable for its courtyard and the intarsia-panelled studiolo, whose wood-inlay designs drew on Botticelli and Francesco di Giorgio Martini. Since 1912 it has housed the National Gallery of the Marche, with paintings including Piero della Francesca's Flagellation and Madonna di Senigallia, Raphael's La Muta, and works by Titian and Paolo Uccello.

palazzo-farnese.name: Farnese Palace, Caprarola
palazzo-farnese.description: Pentagonal Renaissance palace at Caprarola, built between 1559 and 1573 by Jacopo Barozzi da Vignola for Cardinal Alessandro Farnese. It is celebrated for its circular courtyard, the helicoidal Scala Regia ramp designed for riders on horseback, and the frescoed rooms decorated by Taddeo and Federico Zuccari.

palazzo-milzetti-museo-nazionale-dell-et.name: Palazzo Milzetti - National Museum of the Neoclassical Age in Romagna
palazzo-milzetti-museo-nazionale-dell-et.description: Neoclassical palace in Faenza, decorated between 1802 and 1805 by the painter Felice Giani for Count Francesco Milzetti. Its lavishly frescoed rooms, among the finest Neoclassical interiors in Italy, now form the National Museum of the Neoclassical Age in Romagna.

palazzo-reale-di-napoli.name: Royal Palace of Naples
palazzo-reale-di-napoli.description: Former royal residence in Naples, begun in 1600 to a design by Domenico Fontana as the palace of the Spanish viceroys and later home to the Bourbon kings of Naples. Its facade bears eight niche statues of the kings who ruled the city, added in 1888, and its state apartments preserve royal furnishings and a court theatre.

palazzo-simi-centro-operativo-per-l-arch.name: Palazzo Simi – Archaeology Operations Centre
palazzo-simi-centro-operativo-per-l-arch.description: Sixteenth-century noble palace in the old town of Bari, built over the remains of a Byzantine church and earlier Imperial-Roman structures and later owned by the Simi de Burgis family. Since 1999 it has served as the archaeology operations centre of Bari, hosting exhibitions on the city's ancient and medieval past.

pantheon-e-basilica-di-santa-maria-ad-ma.name: Pantheon and Basilica of Santa Maria ad Martyres
pantheon-e-basilica-di-santa-maria-ad-ma.description: Roman temple in the centre of Rome, rebuilt by the emperor Hadrian around 118-125 AD on the site of an earlier building erected by Agrippa in 27 BC. Its coffered concrete dome, still the largest unreinforced dome in the world, is lit by a single oculus; consecrated as a church in 609 AD, the building also holds the tomb of Raphael.

parchi-archeologi-di-crotone-e-sibari-pa.name: Crotone and Sibari Archaeological Parks – Sibari Archaeological Park
parchi-archeologi-di-crotone-e-sibari-pa.description: Archaeological park in Cassano all'Ionio preserving the successive cities on the site: Sybaris, the wealthy Achaean colony founded around 720 BC and destroyed by Croton in 510 BC; Thurii, refounded in 444 BC on a grid plan by the urban planner Hippodamus; and the Roman colony of Copia, established in 194 BC. Systematic excavation began in 1932 and intensified after 1969, uncovering the layered remains of all three settlements.

parchi-archeologici-di-crotone-e-sibari-.name: Crotone and Sibari Archaeological Parks – Le Castella
parchi-archeologici-di-crotone-e-sibari-.description: Coastal promontory in the Capo Rizzuto marine reserve where a Greek defensive wall of the late 4th–early 3rd century BC, possibly linked to ancient Croton, underlies the later fortress. Romans settled colonists here after Hannibal's withdrawal, and the Aragonese castle that gives the site its name took its present form after the fortress was seized by Alfonso V of Aragon in 1444 and rebuilt under Alfonso II by 1487.

parchi-archeologici-di-crotone-e-sibari-.name: Crotone and Sibari Archaeological Parks – National Archaeological Museum of the Sibaritide
parchi-archeologici-di-crotone-e-sibari-.description: Museum at Cassano all'Ionio, between the town of Sibari and the Sybaris archaeological park, opened in the 1990s in a building by architect Riccardo Wallach and enlarged in 2015 by ABDR Architetti Associati. Its collection covers the proto-historic to Roman periods across the successive cities of Sybaris, Thurii and Copia, including Iron Age grave goods from Francavilla Marittima and material from the 6th–4th-century-BC sanctuary of Athena, among it a bronze plaque dedicated by the Olympic victor Kleombrotos.

parchi-archeologici-di-crotone-e-sibari-.name: Crotone and Sibari Archaeological Parks – National Archaeological Museum of Crotone
parchi-archeologici-di-crotone-e-sibari-.description: Museum in Crotone, within the medieval walls that occupy the site of the ancient Greek acropolis of Croton, opened to the public in 1968. The collection ranges from Neolithic and Bronze Age finds to Roman material, and includes Greek pottery, votive objects from the sanctuary of Hera Lacinia at Capo Colonna, and two bronze siren-shaped vessels of which only three examples are known worldwide.

parchi-archeologici-di-crotone-e-sibari-.name: National Archaeological Museum and Park of Capo Colonna
parchi-archeologici-di-crotone-e-sibari-.description: National museum and archaeological park at Capo Colonna, on a promontory near Crotone that was sacred to Hera Lacinia from at least the 8th century BC. Its Doric temple, built around 470 BC over an earlier 7th-century structure, is now reduced to a single standing column about 8 metres tall; the museum displays votive offerings, including precious-metal finds, excavated from the sanctuary.

parchi-archeologici-di-paestum-e-velia-m.name: Paestum and Velia Archaeological Parks - National Archaeological Museum
parchi-archeologici-di-paestum-e-velia-m.description: Archaeological park and museum uniting the Greek cities of Paestum, founded around 600 BC by colonists from Sybaris, and Velia, better known as the birthplace of the Eleatic school of philosophy founded by Parmenides. Paestum preserves three of the best-conserved Doric temples outside Greece, and its museum holds the Tomb of the Diver, the only known Greek painted tomb from the 5th century BC.

parchi-archeologici-di-paestum-e-velia-a.name: Archaeological Area of Velia
parchi-archeologici-di-paestum-e-velia-a.description: Archaeological area of Velia, the ancient Greek city of Elea founded around 540-535 BC by Phocaean refugees, part of the Paestum and Velia Archaeological Parks. Excavated remains include the Porta Rosa gate, the acropolis, Hellenistic and Roman baths, and the agora; Elea was home to the pre-Socratic Eleatic School of philosophy founded by Parmenides and continued by Zeno and Melissus.

parco-reale-e-giardino-inglese-reggia-di.name: Royal Park and English Garden of the Royal Palace of Caserta
parco-reale-e-giardino-inglese-reggia-di.description: Royal park of the Reggia di Caserta, laid out by architect Luigi Vanvitelli from 1752 for the Bourbon king Charles III along a long axis of fountains fed by the Carolino Aqueduct and culminating in the Diana and Actaeon cascade. Within it, Queen Maria Carolina had an English-style garden added from 1786, one of the first in Italy, with exotic plants, small ruins and ponds. The whole complex is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 1997.

parco-archeologica-di-ostia-antica-caste.name: Castle of Julius II
parco-archeologica-di-ostia-antica-caste.description: Fortress at Ostia Antica built 1483-1486 for Cardinal Giuliano della Rovere, the future Pope Julius II, probably to a design by Baccio Pontelli. Its triangular plan with three towers was intended to defend Rome's river approach and control the Tiber grain trade; the interior staircase is decorated with mythological frescoes by Baldassarre Peruzzi. Now part of the Ostia Antica Archaeological Park, it houses a museum.

parco-archeologico-dei-campi-flegrei-anf.name: Flavian Amphitheatre of Pozzuoli
parco-archeologico-dei-campi-flegrei-anf.description: Roman amphitheatre at Puteoli (modern Pozzuoli), built in the second half of the 1st century AD at the colony's own expense, probably under Vespasian and inaugurated under Titus. Measuring about 150 by 116 metres with room for some 40,000 spectators, it was the third-largest in the Roman world after the Colosseum and the amphitheatre of Capua; its well-preserved underground level held the machinery for raising animal cages into the arena. It is part of the Phlegraean Fields Archaeological Park.

parco-archeologico-dei-campi-flegrei-mus.name: Archaeological Museum of the Phlegraean Fields at the Castle of Baia
parco-archeologico-dei-campi-flegrei-mus.description: Archaeological museum of the Phlegraean Fields, opened in 1993 inside the Aragonese Castle of Baia in Bacoli, part of the Phlegraean Fields Archaeological Park. Its topographic displays gather finds from across the area, including the reconstructed facade of the Sacellum of the Augustales from Miseno with statues of Vespasian and Titus, and plaster casts of the submerged nymphaeum of Punta Epitaffio, built for the emperor Claudius and now seven metres underwater because of local ground movement (bradyseism).

parco-archeologico-dei-campi-flegrei-par.name: Phlegraean Fields Archaeological Park - Baths of Baia
parco-archeologico-dei-campi-flegrei-par.description: Archaeological park at Baia, once the most fashionable seaside resort of Roman antiquity, favoured by emperors and the elite for its thermal springs. Its terraced ruins preserve a complex of bath buildings and villas, while a large part of the ancient town now lies submerged offshore in the Bay of Pozzuoli.

parco-archeologico-dei-campi-flegrei-par.name: Phlegraean Fields Archaeological Park - Cumae
parco-archeologico-dei-campi-flegrei-par.description: Archaeological park at Cumae, the first Greek colony founded on the Italian mainland, established around the 8th century BC by settlers from Euboea. The site includes the acropolis with temples to Apollo and Jupiter and the Cave of the Sibyl, a long trapezoidal gallery cut into the rock and associated with the Cumaean Sibyl described by Virgil.

parco-archeologico-del-colosseo-colosseo.name: Colosseum Archaeological Park - Colosseum, Flavian Amphitheatre
parco-archeologico-del-colosseo-colosseo.description: The Flavian Amphitheatre, better known as the Colosseum, built between 70 and 80 AD under the emperors Vespasian and Titus. The largest amphitheatre ever constructed, it could hold tens of thousands of spectators for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles, and remains the defining monument of ancient Rome.

parco-archeologico-del-colosseo-foro-rom.name: Roman Forum and Palatine Hill
parco-archeologico-del-colosseo-foro-rom.description: Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, the political and religious heart of ancient Rome and the hill traditionally linked to the city's founding, later covered with imperial residences. Together with the Colosseum and monuments such as the Arch of Titus and the Arch of Septimius Severus, they form the Colosseum Archaeological Park, established in 2017, one of the most visited archaeological complexes in the world.

parco-archeologico-del-teatro-romano-di-.name: Archaeological Park of the Roman Theatre of Gubbio
parco-archeologico-del-teatro-romano-di-.description: Roman theatre at Gubbio, built in the Augustan period between about 55 and 27 BC, with a cavea that could seat around 6,000 spectators. Excavated from the 15th century onward, with campaigns sponsored by the Gabrielli counts in the 16th century, it preserves its arcaded lower level, part of the upper arcades, and the stage building. A small antiquarium nearby, set in a former Roman house with mosaic floors, displays pre-Roman and Roman finds from the town.

parco-archeologico-del-teatro-e-dell-anf.name: Cividate Camuno Roman Theatre and Amphitheatre Archaeological Park
parco-archeologico-del-teatro-e-dell-anf.description: Archaeological park in Cividate Camuno preserving the Roman theatre and amphitheatre of Civitas Camunnorum, the chief town of the Camunni people in Roman-era Val Camonica. The remains, uncovered through excavation and restoration, are the region's principal evidence of the valley's Roman urban centre.

parco-archeologico-dell-appia-antica-mau.name: Appian Way Archaeological Park - Mausoleum of Cecilia Metella and Church of San Nicola
parco-archeologico-dell-appia-antica-mau.description: Roman mausoleum on the Via Appia Antica, built in the second half of the 1st century BC for Cecilia Metella, daughter of the consul Quintus Caecilius Metellus Creticus. At the end of the 13th century the Caetani family incorporated the tomb into a fortified complex spanning the road, adding the adjoining church of San Nicola, whose walls survive alongside the mausoleum.

parco-archeologico-dell-appia-antica-ant.name: Appian Way Archaeological Park - Antiquarium of Lucrezia Romana
parco-archeologico-dell-appia-antica-ant.description: Small museum on the outskirts of Rome, established in 2015 to house finds from twenty-five years of excavation along the ancient Via Latina in the city's south-eastern suburbs. Its four rooms display material spanning prehistory to the Roman era, including grave goods, mosaics and marble statuary from nearby suburban villas.

parco-archeologico-dell-appia-antica-par.name: Park of the Tombs of the Via Latina and the Basilica of Santo Stefano
parco-archeologico-dell-appia-antica-par.description: Funerary park along the ancient Via Latina in Rome, part of the Appian Way Archaeological Park, preserving a group of tombs of the 2nd century AD, notably the Tomb of the Cornelii (Sepolcro Barberini) with its frescoed and mosaic-floored hypogeum, and the Tomb of the Pancratii with polychrome stucco decoration. The site also contains the Basilica of Santo Stefano, an early Christian church built in the 5th century by Demetrias of the Anicii family, which was a pilgrimage stop until the 13th century.

parco-archeologico-dell-appia-antica-vil.name: Appian Way Archaeological Park - Villa dei Quintili and Santa Maria Nova
parco-archeologico-dell-appia-antica-vil.description: The largest villa on the Via Appia Antica, built in the early 2nd century AD and later owned by the brothers Sextus Quintilius Condianus and Sextus Quintilius Maximus, both consuls in 151 AD. After the emperor Commodus had them executed in 182-183 AD, the estate was confiscated and became an imperial property; excavations have revealed its baths, cisterns and a large nymphaeum, alongside the medieval farmhouse of Santa Maria Nova.

parco-archeologico-dell-appia-antica-vil.name: Appian Way Archaeological Park - Villa di Capo di Bove
parco-archeologico-dell-appia-antica-vil.description: Roman bath complex on the Via Appia Antica, part of a large estate possibly belonging to the 2nd-century sophist Herodes Atticus and his wife Annia Regilla. Acquired by the Italian state in 2002, the site now also houses the archive of the journalist and conservationist Antonio Cederna, a leading campaigner for the protection of the Appian Way.

parco-archeologico-dell-appia-antica-vil.name: Appian Way Archaeological Park - Villa di Sette Bassi
parco-archeologico-dell-appia-antica-vil.description: Large imperial-era villa between the Via Tuscolana and Via Appia, built under Antoninus Pius (138-161 AD) and occupied into the 4th century. The 37,000-square-metre complex included three residential blocks around a portico and a hippodrome-shaped garden nearly 330 metres long, its dramatic four-storey facade surviving until it collapsed in a storm in 1951.

parco-archeologico-dell-area-urbana-e-de.name: Archaeological Park of the Urban Area and Crucinia Necropolis of Metaponto
parco-archeologico-dell-area-urbana-e-de.description: Archaeological park protecting part of the urban area and the Crucinia necropolis of ancient Metapontum, an Achaean Greek colony founded on the Ionian coast of Basilicata in the second half of the 7th century BC at Sybaris's initiative. The philosopher Pythagoras is said to have settled and taught in the city after leaving Croton. The park preserves traces of the ancient street grid and houses, alongside burials from one of the city's cemetery areas.

parco-archeologico-di-aeclanum.name: Aeclanum Archaeological Park
parco-archeologico-di-aeclanum.description: Archaeological park near Mirabella Eclano preserving Aeclanum, a Samnite settlement that became a Roman municipium after the Social War of 91-88 BC and received colony status under Hadrian around 120 AD. The 18-hectare site retains stretches of city wall over ten metres high, public baths, a circular market building and a late antique basilica.

parco-archeologico-di-altino.name: Archaeological Park of Altino
parco-archeologico-di-altino.description: Archaeological park of Altinum, a Veneti settlement that grew into a major Roman port city linking the Adriatic to routes across the eastern Alps, reaching municipal status by the mid-1st century BC. Aerial surveys in 2007-2009 revealed its full street grid beneath the fields, along with a theatre and an amphitheatre measuring roughly 500 by 370 Roman feet; finds from the site are displayed in the National Archaeological Museum of Altino, founded in 1960. Long linked to legends of Venice's founding after Attila's attack in 452, the city in fact survived for centuries afterward.

parco-archeologico-di-amiternum.name: Archaeological Park of Amiternum
parco-archeologico-di-amiternum.description: Archaeological park of Amiternum, an ancient Sabine town about 11 km north of L'Aquila that became a Roman municipium and the birthplace, around 86 BC, of the historian Sallust. Visible remains include an Augustan-period theatre and a 1st-century AD amphitheatre that could hold up to about 6,000 spectators, along with traces of a domestic villa with mosaics and stretches of the Via Caecilia.

parco-archeologico-di-canne-della-battag.name: Cannae Archaeological Park and Antiquarium
parco-archeologico-di-canne-della-battag.description: Site of the Battle of Cannae (216 BC), where Hannibal's Carthaginian army inflicted one of Rome's heaviest defeats of the Second Punic War. The hilltop settlement of Canne was occupied from the Bronze Age through the Middle Ages, and its remains include the San Mercurio baths and a medieval citadel. The Antiquarium, inaugurated in 1958 by future prime minister Aldo Moro, displays prehistoric, Daunian, Roman and medieval finds from the site.

parco-archeologico-di-casinum-e-museo-ar.name: Casinum Archaeological Park and "Gianfilippo Carettoni" National Archaeological Museum
parco-archeologico-di-casinum-e-museo-ar.description: Remains of Casinum, a Volscian and later Samnite settlement absorbed by Rome in the 3rd century BC, near modern Cassino at the foot of Montecassino abbey; visible remains include megalithic walls, a Roman theatre, an amphitheatre for roughly 4,000 spectators, and the funerary monument of Ummidia Quadratilla. The adjoining museum, opened in 1979 and named in 2003 after archaeologist Gianfilippo Carettoni, displays prehistoric, Roman and funerary finds from the area, including a late-Republican marble statue and a decorated bone funerary bed from Aquinum.

parco-archeologico-di-cerveteri-e-tarqui.name: National Archaeological Museum of Tarquinia
parco-archeologico-di-cerveteri-e-tarqui.description: Etruscan collection housed in the 15th-century Palazzo Vitelleschi in Tarquinia's historic centre; the museum was founded in 1924. Holdings include frescoes and reconstructed tomb chambers removed from the nearby Monterozzi necropolis, among them the Triclinium and Leopards tombs, alongside the 3rd-century-BC Sarcophagus of the Obese. It ranks among Italy's foremost collections devoted to Etruscan civilization.

parco-archeologico-di-cerveteri-e-tarqui.name: Cerveteri and Tarquinia Archaeological Park - Cerite National Archaeological Museum
parco-archeologico-di-cerveteri-e-tarqui.description: Archaeological park uniting the Etruscan necropolises of Cerveteri, above all the Banditaccia necropolis with its rows of tumulus tombs carved to resemble houses, and those of Tarquinia, jointly inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2004. The associated Museo Nazionale Cerite, in Cerveteri's medieval castle, displays finds excavated from the tombs.

parco-archeologico-di-cerveteri-e-tarqui.name: Monterozzi Necropolis, Tarquinia
parco-archeologico-di-cerveteri-e-tarqui.description: Etruscan burial ground on a ridge outside Tarquinia, in use from the late 7th to the 2nd century BC and renowned for the largest surviving body of Etruscan painted tomb art. Rock-cut chamber tombs are decorated with frescoes of banquets, dancers, musicians and funerary games, among them the Tomb of the Leopards, the Tomb of Hunting and Fishing, and the Tomb of the Augurs. A UNESCO World Heritage site since 2004, together with the Banditaccia necropolis at Cerveteri.

parco-archeologico-di-cerveteri-e-tarqui.name: Banditaccia Necropolis
parco-archeologico-di-cerveteri-e-tarqui.description: Etruscan necropolis of the ancient city of Caere, northwest of Cerveteri, in use from the 9th to the 2nd century BC and covering some 20 hectares, one of the largest burial grounds of the ancient Mediterranean. Tombs range from Villanovan pit and trench graves to large circular tumuli cut into the tufa and, later, cube-shaped 'dado' tombs lining street grids that mimic the layout of a town, among them the Tomb of the Reliefs with its painted stucco furnishings. A UNESCO World Heritage site since 2004, together with the Monterozzi necropolis at Tarquinia.

parco-archeologico-di-ercolano-area-arch.name: Herculaneum
parco-archeologico-di-ercolano-area-arch.description: Roman town buried, along with Pompeii, under volcanic material during the 79 AD eruption of Vesuvius; unlike Pompeii's ash and pumice, Herculaneum's deposits of hot mud and pyroclastic flow hardened around timber, furniture and food, preserving organic remains in exceptional condition. Discovered by chance in 1709 and excavated systematically from 1738, notably under Amedeo Maiuri from 1927, the site includes richly decorated houses, public baths, and the Villa of the Papyri with its carbonized library of scrolls. A UNESCO World Heritage site since 1997, together with Pompeii and Oplontis.

parco-archeologico-di-grumentum.name: Grumentum Archaeological Park
parco-archeologico-di-grumentum.description: Remains of Grumentum, a Roman city founded in the 3rd century BC in Lucania as a military outpost during the Samnite Wars. It was the site of two battles of the Second Punic War (215 and 207 BC), in which Hannibal, encamped near the walls, was eventually defeated by Gaius Claudius Nero. Visible ruins include an Augustan-era theatre, a 1st-century-BC amphitheatre, the forum, thermal baths and an aqueduct, excavated systematically from the 1950s under Pellegrino Claudio Sestieri.

parco-archeologico-di-herakleia.name: Herakleia Archaeological Park
parco-archeologico-di-herakleia.description: Archaeological park at Policoro on the site of Heraclea, founded around 434 BC by colonists from Taras and Thurii on the earlier settlement of Siris. It became capital of the Italiote League by 374 BC and, in 280 BC, was the site of the battle where Pyrrhus first deployed war elephants against a Roman army; the acropolis preserves temples and a grid of paved streets, with finds displayed in the National Archaeological Museum of Siritide.

parco-archeologico-di-iuvanum.name: Iuvanum Archaeological Park
parco-archeologico-di-iuvanum.description: Archaeological park at Montenerodomo on a plateau in the Maiella mountains, site of Iuvanum, chief town of the Samnite Carricini people from at least the 4th-3rd century BC and reorganised as a Roman municipium in the mid-1st century BC. The site preserves a Samnite sanctuary with twin temples and a small theatre, alongside the Roman forum and baths, with finds displayed in a museum opened in 2006.

parco-archeologico-di-minturnae-e-ponte-.name: Minturnae Archaeological Park and Ponte Real Ferdinando
parco-archeologico-di-minturnae-e-ponte-.description: Archaeological park at Minturno preserving Minturnae, a Roman colony founded in 295 BC on the right bank of the Garigliano, on the Via Appia. Visible remains include a theatre built to seat over 4,000 spectators, the forum, an eleven-kilometre aqueduct and a macellum, complemented nearby by the Ponte Real Ferdinando, an iron chain suspension bridge built in 1828-1832 by the engineer Luigi Giura, among the first of its kind in Italy.

parco-archeologico-di-monte-sannace.name: Monte Sannace Archaeological Park
parco-archeologico-di-monte-sannace.description: Archaeological park on a hilltop near Gioia del Colle preserving a fortified settlement of the ancient Peucetians, inhabited from the 10th century BCE and enclosed from the late 4th century BCE by defensive walls that separated an acropolis from the lower town. Excavated from 1929 by Michele Gervasio and resumed in the 1960s, the site flourished during the Hellenistic period before its occupation faded under Roman rule.

parco-archeologico-di-ostia-antica-area-.name: Ostia Antica Archaeological Area
parco-archeologico-di-ostia-antica-area-.description: Extensive archaeological area preserving Rome's ancient harbour city, founded according to tradition in the 7th century BCE at the mouth of the Tiber and grown into a major port and trading hub under the Empire. Its ruins, abandoned after the river silted up and the coastline receded, include the forum, theatre, warehouses, baths and multi-storey apartment blocks that make it one of the best-preserved Roman towns.

parco-archeologico-di-ostia-antica-compl.name: Imperial Ports of Claudius and Trajan (Portus)
parco-archeologico-di-ostia-antica-compl.description: Remains of Portus, the artificial harbour Rome built on the coast north of Ostia to receive grain and goods shipped from across the empire. Claudius began the outer harbour around AD 46, its two long moles and lighthouse completed and inaugurated by Nero in AD 54; Trajan then added an inner hexagonal basin, designed by Apollodorus of Damascus and finished around AD 112, whose 32-hectare outline is still clearly traceable on the ground and from the air. A canal, the Fossa Traiana, connected the port complex to the Tiber and to Ostia.

parco-archeologico-di-ostia-antica-museo.name: Museum of Roman Ships
parco-archeologico-di-ostia-antica-museo.description: Museum near Fiumicino airport built to house five Roman vessels unearthed between 1958 and 1961 during the airport's construction, in what had been the harbour basins of Claudius and Trajan. Alongside the excavated cargo barges, a sailing ship and a fishing boat, it displays anchors, amphorae and inscriptions recovered from ancient Portus; closed for restoration in 2002, it reopened to the public in 2021.

parco-archeologico-di-ostia-antica-necro.name: Isola Sacra Necropolis
parco-archeologico-di-ostia-antica-necro.description: Roman necropolis on the artificial island formed between the Tiber and the Fossa Traiana, serving the port communities of Ostia and Portus between the 1st and 4th centuries CE. Discovered by chance in 1925 during land reclamation, its roughly two hundred tombs range from simple coffins to house-like family mausolea and preserve a wealth of inscriptions and mosaics documenting the lives of freedmen and port workers.

parco-archeologico-di-pompei-antiquarium.name: Antiquarium of Boscoreale
parco-archeologico-di-pompei-antiquarium.description: Museum in Boscoreale, opened in 1991, devoted to daily life, agriculture and viticulture in the Vesuvian countryside before the eruption of AD 79. Its collection, drawn from villas and farms in the area, part of the wider Pompeii Archaeological Park network, includes tools, food remains, an animal cast with its collar, and material from the Villa della Pisanella, notably a scale model of its wine cellar holding 84 storage jars. Nearby stands Villa Regina, the only Roman farm villa in the area to have been fully excavated and reconstructed.

parco-archeologico-di-pompei-area-archeo.name: Pompeii Archaeological Area
parco-archeologico-di-pompei-area-archeo.description: The ruins of the Roman town of Pompeii, buried under ash and pumice by the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 CE and rediscovered through excavations beginning in the 18th century. Its streets, houses, forum, theatres and amphitheatre, remarkably preserved by the volcanic deposits, offer the most complete surviving picture of daily life in a Roman city and were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1997.

parco-archeologico-di-pompei-reggia-del-.name: Quisisana Palace - Libero D'Orsi Archaeological Museum of Stabiae
parco-archeologico-di-pompei-reggia-del-.description: Museum at Castellammare di Stabia named after Libero D'Orsi, the schoolteacher-turned-archaeologist whose excavations from 1950 uncovered the luxury Roman villas of ancient Stabiae, a seaside resort destroyed alongside Pompeii by the 79 CE eruption of Vesuvius. Housed in the former Aragonese royal hunting lodge of Quisisana, it displays frescoes, mosaics and finds from Villa San Marco and Villa Arianna.

parco-archeologico-di-pompei-scavi-arche.name: Villa Arianna
